grades_v0.reason: E08 gives a QBiC-SELEX prediction only (z 33.95, alt binds more, own model). RELA is picked on expression (73 TPM), which is a reasonable rationale, but there is no ChIP or allelic evidence.
E03 shows no cCRE within 500 bp and the nearest is 1.5 kb away (H3K4me3 promoter-like). E01 shows no regulatory feature. Nothing supports an enhancer here; the claim is speculation.
E02 only lists CYP7A1 at 927 kb. Distance is not evidence of regulation. There is no eQTL, no looping data and no Hi-C. Calling CYP7A1 the only LDL-relevant gene is not shown by the evidence.
E08 shows RELA at 73 TPM in Hep3B, so it is expressed. Expression is permissive only. NF-kB activity depends on stimulation, and there is no chromatin evidence here.
No evidence is cited. The claim that NF-kB represses CYP7A1 and raises LDL comes from memory. The direction chain also needs the variant to have an LDL association, and E04/E05 show none.

E10 is a prediction only. The group has mixed directions: SETBP1 is opposite and HMGA1 is the own-model best. HMGA1 is a plausible pick by expression (239 TPM), but HMGA1 binds AT-rich DNA nonspecifically, so the QBiC z score is not very informative.
E03 and E01 show no cCRE. The claim that HMGA1 acts outside the registry is an assertion with no evidence cited.

The claim that the variant lies within the intronic neighbourhood of FAM110B is contradicted by E02: FAM110B is 420.6 kb upstream of the variant, and E01 says there are no transcript consequences (intergenic) while also saying the consequence is intron_variant, which is inconsistent. There is no eQTL or contact evidence.
E10 shows HMGA1 at 239 TPM in Hep3B, so it is expressed. That is only permissive.
E06 is a pravastatin response study returned by a keyword search. It is not shown to implicate FAM110B in LDL, and it is not evidence for this variant or gene. No direction is given.

E16 gives four concordant TEAD models, but they are paralogs with near-identical motifs, so this is not independent confirmation. Prediction only. TEAD1 is chosen as best-scoring, but TEAD2 has the highest expression.
Concordant paralog models are not evidence of an enhancer. E03 shows no cCRE nearby.
E02 shows only that CYP7A1 is in the window, 927 kb away. The TEAD/YAP claim on bile acid genes is uncited and there is no linking data.
E16 supports TEAD1-4 expression of 17-34 TPM in Hep3B, which is permissive only.
No evidence cited. The claim of YAP/TEAD suppression of CYP7A1 and a rise in LDL is from memory, and there is no variant-level LDL association (E04/E05).

E11 is a prediction only (z -29.06, alt binds less). Direction is consistent with allele_binding_more=ref. ZNF580 is picked as the strongest loss at a single-model group, with no reason beyond its z score.
E03 shows no cCRE nearby. The claim that loss of an occupied site matters assumes occupancy that is not shown. The text claims de-repression of an element that is not identified.
E02 lists FAM110B as nearest at 420 kb, which is far away. Proximity is not evidence for regulation and no eQTL is cited.
E11 shows ZNF580 at 8.5 TPM in Hep3B. Expressed at a low level; permissive only.
E06 is a pharmacogenomic statin paper and does not tie FAM110B or this variant to LDL. The claimed effect direction on LDL is not stated.

grades_final.reason: E08 gives an in vitro RELA own-model prediction (z 33.95, alt binds more) and the RELA choice is justified by expression. This is a binding prediction alone, and E19 shows no RELA peak in HepG2. E19 is HepG2, not Hep3B, so it is only a weak negative.
E03 shows no cCRE overlap (nearest 1544 bp away) and E01 shows no regulatory feature. Nothing cited demonstrates an element, as the chain itself concedes.
CYP7A1 is 927 kb away (E02) and E18 shows no eQTL. It was picked for LDL plausibility, with no contact or perturbation data.
E08 shows RELA at 73.4 TPM in this line, which is permissive expression only. Stimulation-dependent activity is not shown, and E19 gives no occupancy in HepG2.

E20 reports no CYP7A1 association, and E04 and E05 give no GWAS or Open Targets record for the variant. The chain concedes the direction to higher LDL is asserted. CYP7A1 coverage is not shown to be tied to this variant.

E10 gives an HMGA1 own-model prediction (z 29.74, alt binds more). The group disagrees in direction (SETBP1 negative), and HMGA1 has low sequence specificity. This is a prediction only, with no ChIP or perturbation support.
E03 shows no cCRE overlap and E01 shows no regulatory feature. No element is shown.
FAM110B is assigned by proximity alone, 420.6 kb from the TSS (E02), with no eQTL (E18) and no contact data.
E10 shows HMGA1 at 239 TPM in the line, which is permissive expression only. No chromatin or occupancy data are cited.
E06 is a keyword hit on a pravastatin pharmacogenomics paper and does not link FAM110B to LDL. E04 has no association, so no direction is supported.

E11 gives a ZNF580 own-model prediction of reduced alt binding (z -29.06, ref site at the 100th percentile). This is a prediction only, with no ChIP or allelic data. The direction is consistent with allele_binding_more being ref.
E03 shows no cCRE overlap and E01 shows no regulatory feature. Occupancy of the site is not shown.
No target gene is specified. E18 shows no eQTL and the nearest gene is 420.6 kb away (E02).
E11 shows ZNF580 at 8.5 TPM in the line, which is permissive expression only.
E04 and E05 show no GWAS or Open Targets record, so no LDL link or direction is shown.

E12 gives an NME2 own-model prediction (z 28.95, alt binds more) with a modest effect (0.573). This is an in vitro prediction only. NME2 is a ubiquitous nucleoside diphosphate kinase and not a typical sequence-specific regulator, so binding relevance is doubtful.
E03 shows no cCRE overlap and E01 shows no regulatory feature. No element is shown.
No target gene is named. E18 shows no eQTL and all candidate genes are at least 420 kb away (E02).
E12 shows NME2 at 928 TPM in the line, which is permissive expression only. It shows no functional activity at this site.
E04 and E05 show no GWAS or Open Targets record, so no LDL connection is shown.

next_experiment: Cheapest separating test beyond existing data: a dual-luciferase allelic reporter of the 200 bp window around chr8:57573391 (ref G vs alt T) in Hep 3B2.1-7, assayed unstimulated and after TNF. No allelic difference in either condition supports H0 (currently the leading chain); a TNF-dependent difference supports H1, and a stimulation-independent difference points to H2, H4 or H5, to be resolved by the subsequent EMSA/supershift and knockdown panel.
